0|a9701a30470856408d08657eb1bd7ae29a146190|torvalds~linux|/home/usuario01/Titan-Files-Research/src/_00/output/C/torvalds~linux|False|"[PATCH] md: support BIO_RW_BARRIER for md/raid1
We can only accept BARRIER requests if all slaves handle
barriers
So we keep track of whether the whole array seems safe for barriers
and also whether each individual rdev handles barriers.
We initially assumes barriers are OK.
When writing the superblock we try a barrier
things for no-barriers.  This will usually clear the flags fairly quickly.
If writing the superblock finds that BIO_RW_BARRIER is -ENOTSUPP
resubmit
column2: so introduce function ""md_super_wait"" which waits for requests to

column1: finish
column2: and retries ENOTSUPP requests without the barrier flag.

column1: When writing the real raid1
column2: write requests which were BIO_RW_BARRIER but

column1: which aresn't supported need to be retried.  So raid1d is enhanced to do this
and when any bio write completes (i.e.  no retry needed) we remove it from the
r1bio
column2: so that devices needing retry are easy to find.

column1: We should hardly ever get -ENOTSUPP errors when writing data to the raid.
It should only happen if:
1/ the device used to support BARRIER
change like this
or
2/ the array has no persistent superblock
column2: so there was no opportunity to

column1: pre-test for barriers when writing the superblock.
